findings.description: The user_data script contains a plaintext AWS access key and secret access key. This exposes long-lived credentials to anyone with access to the instance metadata, Terraform state, or console describe-instance-attribute calls, enabling account compromise.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data at rest on the volume is stored unencrypted, risking exposure if the underlying storage is accessed or snapshots are shared.

The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and does not enable encryption itself, meaning the snapshot data at rest is unprotected and could be exposed if the snapshot is inadvertently shared publicly.

The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) and port 80 (HTTP) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management interface to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploitation attempts against SSH.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing the exposed attack surface for the associated EC2 instance.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to any instance launched in this subnet, unnecessarily expanding the internet-facing attack surface.

findings.issue_category: missing bucket encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket used for VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, no public access block, and no policy restricting access, risking unauthorized access to or tampering with sensitive network flow log data.
